newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end flat, spreads to U.S. narrow.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end flat, spreads to U.S. narrow.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in quiet trade on Wednesday, outperforming softer U.S. Treasuries, as the market held firm after the Canadian currency failed to break through a key support level.

"The fact that the dollar didn't break through C$1.38 I think was seen as a near term positive," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs. "After considerable international selling (of bonds) over the last couple of days, it dried up a little bit today."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.02 to C$108.82 to yield 7.242 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 10/32 to yield 6.99 percent. The spread between the two narrowed to 25 basis points from 28 basis points at Tuesday's close.

Canada's bond market outperformance followed a sudden widening of spreads in the previous session, when Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen told a Senate committee that the central bank now has greater flexibility to resist a U.S. rate hike.
"The activity in the Canadian market was just the aftermath of yesterday's underperformance. It attracted some buyers," said Salomon Brothers economist Anita Lauria.
Lauria said the underlying sentiment among investors is that while both currency and bond market are vulnerable to a near term to a Fed tightening, they are well supported on a fundamental basis.

Canada's dollar ended weaker but recouped some of its early losses on Wednesday as jitters over the direction of U.S. interest rates weighed on the currency. The unit failed to break through the key C$1.3800 (US$0.7246) level.
Canadian bond investors will now focus on tomorrow's testimony by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan before the Joint Economic Committee on Monetary Policy, said Chandler.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.02 to C$102.73 to yield 6.612. The U.S. bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.74 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 13 basis points from 11 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.14 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.29 percent.
